simple.meaning: רָדַד (râdad) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “to tread in pieces, i.e. (figuratively) to conquer , or (specifically) to overlay.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 4 times across Judges, 1 Kings, Psalms, Isaiah, beginning at Judges 19:11. Its contexts include kingship, city.

definitions.short: to tread in pieces, i.e. (figuratively) to conquer , or (specifically) to overlay
definitions.full: H7286. radad [ רָדַד ] verb beat out , figurative beat down, subdue (Late Hebrew Pi`el stamp or beat down, make flat, spread out ; רְדַד ᵑ7 beat out ; compare probably Arabic repel, reject (Nö M 75 ); Assyrian radâdu is pursue (rare)); — Qal , figurative, beat down: Infinitive construct גּוֺיִם לְפָנָיו לְרַד Isa 45:1 ; Participle active תַּחְתָּ֑י עַמִּי הָרוֺדֵד Psa 144:2 ; — so also Imperfect יָרֹד Isa 41:2 accusative Ew and others (for יַרְדְּ ᵑ0 , see I. רדה Hiph`il ). — Judg 19:11 read יָרַד . Hiph`il literally beat out: Imperfect 3masculine singular אֶתהַֿזָּהָב ֗֗֗ עַלהַֿכְּרוּבִים וַיָּ֫רֶד 1Kin 6:32 and beat out the gold upon the cherubim (covered them with beaten gold).

occurrences.englishText: When they were by Jebus, the day was far spent; and the servant said to his master, “Please come and let’s enter into this city of the Jebusites, and stay in it.”
So he made two doors of olive wood; and he carved on them carvings of cherubim, palm trees, and open flowers, and overlaid them with gold. He spread the gold on the cherubim and on the palm trees.
Yahweh says to his anointed, to Cyrus, whose right hand I have held, to subdue nations before him, and strip kings of their armor; to open the doors before him, and the gates shall not be shut:
